title: Generic smooth centers and completed normal coordinates
statement:
Let $Z$ be smooth of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, let $E$ be a finite ordered simple normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], and let $N_1,\ldots,N_s\hookrightarrow Z$, $s\ge1$, be smooth closed subschemes to which $E$ is transverse: boundary equations through a point restrict to distinct members of a regular parameter system on each $N_j$. Fix $x\in\bigcap_jN_j$. For each $j$ fix a coherent ideal $I_j\subseteq\mathcal O_{N_j}$ and an integer $d_j\ge1$ such that $(I_j)_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_{N_j,x}^{d_j}$. After replacing $Z$ by an open neighbourhood of $x$, the reduced closure $T=\overline{\{x\}}_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a smooth closed subscheme of every $N_j$ and of $Z$, lies in every boundary component through $x$, meets no other boundary component, and has normal crossings with $E$. In each $N_j$, the ideal of $T$ is locally generated by a subset of etale coordinates, including equations of all boundary components through $x$, and $I_j\subseteq\mathcal I_{T,N_j}^{d_j}$. If $(I_j)_x=0$, one may arrange $I_j=0$ near $T$.
Put $F=\kappa(x)$ and $n_j=\dim\mathcal O_{N_j,x}$. The completed local ring at $x$ has a coefficient field $F$ and is isomorphic to $F[[u_1,\ldots,u_{n_j}]]$, with any chosen regular parameter system, including the boundary equations, mapped to the variables. Extension to this completion preserves containment in powers of the maximal ideal and of any chosen boundary parameter, and detects the zero ideal. For the coordinate blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup] charts of the pair $(N_j,T)$, and for products with affine space, completion at the generic points of the corresponding coordinate sections gives the usual coordinate substitutions with these coefficients fixed. These assertions include $n_j=0$ and nonclosed $x$. Smoothness, finite type, closed immersion, coherent ideals, etale coordinates and completion use [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Here normal crossings of the flag $(N_j,T,E)$ means the simultaneous etale flag coordinates of [def-trf-etale-coordinate-flag]; regular systems of parameters, residue fields and Krull dimension use [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], [def-weil-residue-field] and [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Agent simultaneous-normal-slice formulation using Tag 0B8X (lemma-dense-smooth-open-variety-over-perfect-field); more-morphisms.tex Tag 0FUE (lemma-etale-local-structure); algebra.tex Tags 0C0S (lemma-regular-complete-containing-coefficient-field) and 00MC (lemma-completion-faithfully-flat). Includes spreading along the reduced closure of a point and the coordinate-chart completion comparison, not stated verbatim by any one of those tags.

proof.text: Work first in an affine neighbourhood $Z=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$, with prime $\mathfrak p$ corresponding to $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], $T=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak p)$ is its reduced closure. The ideals of every $N_j$ and every boundary component containing $x$ lie in $\mathfrak p$, so $T$ is a closed subscheme of each of them, scheme-theoretically. Remove all boundary components not containing $x$; their finite union is closed and misses $x$. Shrinking again always replaces $T$ by its intersection with that open. In $\mathcal O_{N_j,x}$ its ideal is the maximal ideal, and its residue field is $F=\kappa(x)$.

The ring $A/\mathfrak p$ is a nonzero finite-type domain over $\mathbf Q$. Its fraction field is separable over $\mathbf Q$ by [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-separable]. Apply [lem-exc-generic-smooth-domain] to obtain a nonzero $g\in A/\mathfrak p$ with $(A/\mathfrak p)_g$ smooth over $\mathbf Q$. This gives a smooth scheme by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]. Lift $g$ to $A$ and restrict $Z$ to its principal open. The generic point $x$ remains and the entire resulting $T$ is smooth. This is the generic-smooth-open assertion, not an assumption that the original closure was smooth. Ambient and support local rings are Noetherian regular by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular].

source.place: Tag 07ND (lemma-smooth-at-generic-point); varieties.tex Tag 0B8X; characteristic-zero separability and generic localization.

proof.text: Spread the ideal containments before taking completions. Locally each $I_j$ has finitely many section generators, by [pqf-def-coherent]. On an affine neighbourhood in $N_j$, let $P_j$ be the ideal of $T$. For each generator $g$ the hypothesis gives an expression for $g_x$ as a finite sum of products of $d_j$ elements of $(P_j)_x$, with coefficients in $\mathcal O_{N_j,x}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], represent those elements and coefficients by fractions of sections, with denominators outside the prime of $x$. Clear these finitely many denominators. The difference between the two sides is zero in the stalk, so that same lemma supplies one further denominator killing it. Multiplying over the finite generator list gives an open containing $x$ on which $I_j\subseteq P_j^{d_j}$. If $(I_j)_x=0$, apply its zero-germ criterion directly to the generators to obtain $I_j=0$. Each support open comes from an ambient open; intersect these finitely many ambient opens. The containments now hold on the whole shrunken supports, hence near their common $T$.

source.place: Tag 01Y3 (lemma-local-isomorphism), stalk-zero argument written explicitly by clearing finitely many denominators.

proof.text: Construct the flag coordinates separately for each $j$; a common coordinate system for all the $N_j$ is not needed. Fix $N=N_j$ and write $h_1,\ldots,h_n$ for a regular parameter system of $\mathcal O_{N,x}$ beginning with the restricted boundary equations through $x$; this is possible by the transversality hypothesis. Since the ideal of $T$ has stalk $\mathfrak m_{N,x}$, choose representatives of the remaining $h_i$ in that ideal on a neighbourhood. They generate it after shrinking: express a finite set of its generators in terms of the $h_i$ at $x$ and clear denominators as in step 3. The finite set exists since $N$ is locally Noetherian. By [lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates] for $N\hookrightarrow Z$, choose regular equations $a_1,\ldots,a_c$ for $N$ near $x$. Lift the $h_i$ to $Z$, retaining the original ambient boundary equations for the prescribed initial entries. On smooth $T$, choose an etale coordinate tuple $t_1,\ldots,t_b$ by [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form], and lift it to $Z$. Then the ideals of $N,T$ are respectively $(a)$ and $(a,h)$ near $x$.

source.place: Tag 0FUE (lemma-etale-local-structure), adapted coordinate construction; prescribed boundary equations retained among h.

proof.text: The tuple $(a,h,t)$ is etale after a further shrink. Indeed apply [lem-pur-conormal-sequence-smooth-immersion] first to $T\hookrightarrow N$ and then to $N\hookrightarrow Z$. At $x$ the first conormal fibre is $\mathfrak m_{N,x}/\mathfrak m_{N,x}^2$, with basis the $h_i$. The second has basis the $a_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free], since these are the regular equations supplied in step 4. On $T$, the $dt_i$ are a differential basis by [lem-trf-etale-coordinate-derivations-jacobian]. Exactness of the two conormal sequences therefore shows that $da,dh,dt$ form an $F$-basis of $\Omega_{Z/\mathbf Q}\otimes F$: project a relation first to $\Omega_N$, then to $\Omega_T$, to kill its coefficients in reverse order; lift a vector along the same two surjections to see spanning. Apply [lem-pur-etale-at-point-from-differentials] on the smooth finite-type $\mathbf Q$-scheme $Z$. The resulting etale map has $N,T$ as coordinate subspaces and all the retained boundary components as distinct coordinate hyperplanes. No identification of the residue field with $\mathbf Q$ was made.

source.place: Tags 06AA (lemma-differentials-relative-immersion-smooth) and 02GU (lemma-etale-at-point); algebra.tex regular-sequence conormal basis. Two exact sequences and elementary basis lifting.

proof.text: Intersect the finitely many neighbourhoods from steps 4--5. Each of their coordinate maps remains etale on this intersection. For each $j$, take its own tuple $(a,h,t)$, with index sets for $(a)$ contained in those for $(a,h)$. Assign each surviving boundary label its prescribed $h_i$. This gives exactly [def-trf-etale-coordinate-flag]; at points outside $N_j$ or $T$, restrict further to their open complements as required by that definition. All omitted boundary components have unit ideal by step 1. Thus $T$ has the asserted normal crossings for every flag. In particular in $N_j$ its ideal is generated by the $h_i$, including the boundary equations. Finiteness of $s$ is precisely what lets all restrictions be made in one ambient neighbourhood.

source.place: Tag 0FUE (lemma-etale-local-structure); elementary assembly of the finitely many adapted coordinate maps.

proof.text: Fix $j$ and put $R=\mathcal O_{N_j,x}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_{N_j,x}$, $n=n_j$. This is a nonzero Noetherian regular local ring by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]. Its maximal-ideal completion $H$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mH$ and residue field $F$ by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], regular by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local], and has dimension $n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension]. The images of every chosen regular parameter system of $R$ generate $\mathfrak mH$. These conclusions apply to nonclosed $x$, since each cited theorem is about arbitrary Noetherian local rings.

source.place: Tags 07NY (lemma-completion-regular), 07NV (lemma-completion-dimension); algebra.tex Tags 0316 and 05GI for the completed ring.

proof.text: The residue field $F$ has characteristic zero. The ring $H$ is $\mathfrak mH$-adically complete by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] ($\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated), so both results below apply to it. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-coefficient-ring-exists] to $H$: its coefficient ring is a field mapping isomorphically onto $F$. Inverting that residue isomorphism gives a specified section $c:F\to H$. For any of the parameter systems in step 7, [lem-trf-regular-complete-coefficient-coordinates] now gives the continuous isomorphism $F[[U_1,\ldots,U_n]]\to H$ with $U_i\mapsto u_i$ and constants mapped by $c$. Its inverse is the asserted parameter-to-variable identification. The field section is chosen, not claimed canonical, and may be used with every prescribed parameter system. In particular the boundary equations can be sent to their corresponding variables.

source.place: Tags 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem), characteristic-zero coefficient-ring case, and 0C0S (lemma-regular-complete-containing-coefficient-field), clause (2).

proof.text: The map $R\to H$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]. For any ideal $L\subseteq R$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] to $R/L$. Identifying $(R/L)\otimes_RH$ with $H/LH$ by $\overline r\otimes h\mapsto rh\bmod LH$ (inverse $h\mapsto\overline1\otimes h$) gives $LH\cap R=L$. Consequently for ideals $K,L$, $KH\subseteq LH$ if and only if $K\subseteq L$. Take $L=\mathfrak m^q$ and $L=(u_i)^q$; extension of either power is the power of the extended ideal, by expanding its finite products. Take $L=0$ to detect the zero ideal. Thus both the ordinary order and every boundary divisibility are preserved and reflected; no inference from flatness alone to ideal contraction is used.

source.place: Tags 00MC (lemma-completion-faithfully-flat) and 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective); ideal-contraction argument on the quotient module.

proof.text:
Identify the actual charts before completing. On an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset N_j$, with center ideal $P$, the chart cover is [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover]. Write $x=\mathfrak p$ and $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$. Localization of the chart $A[P/a]\subseteq A_a$ at $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ is $R[PR/a]$: send each coefficient fraction and each generator $p/a$ to the same fraction in $R_a$; the inverse sends $(p/s)/a$ to $(p/a)/s$. The defining equality of fractions makes both maps well defined. This uses the fraction construction [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], rather than an uncited base-change assertion. Since $PR=\mathfrak m_R$, take as generators of $P$ the coordinates $h_1,\ldots,h_n$ of step 6, which generate $P$ on the shrunken affine and are a regular parameter system $u_1,\ldots,u_n$ of $R$. For $n>0$, any ordering beginning with its pivot $u_a$ is a regular sequence by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence]. Therefore [lem-trf-blowup-chart-regular-sequence-presentation] identifies its chart with $R[y_i:i
e a]/(u_i-u_a y_i:i
e a)$. The generic coordinate section is the point with ideal $(u_a,y_i:i
e a)$ and residue $F$.

source.place: Tag 0804 (lemma-blowing-up-affine); regular-sequence chart presentation and elementary localization of its fraction algebra.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-parameter-chart-completion-substitution] to the ring and section identified in step 10, with $r=0$ and $J=\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Its completion is $F[[e,Y_i:i\ne a]]$, and the actual completed pullback is $u_a\mapsto e$, $u_i\mapsto eY_i$. Its coefficient section is the composite of $c$ with that completed local map, so the formula fixes the chosen $F$. For a product $N_j\times\mathbf A^r$, localize its polynomial coordinate ring along the generic zero section. This is precisely the $J=\varnothing$ case of the same lemma and gives $F[[u_1,\ldots,u_n,t_1,\ldots,t_r]]$. Taking a coordinate center $(v_i:i\in J)$ in this product gives its nonempty subset $J$ case, including centers cut out by boundary parameters: localize the chart at $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ as in step 10; order $v_J$ with the pivot $v_a$ first, then the other $u_i$, then the other $t_i$. The $u$'s in any order are a regular sequence in $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], hence in the free $R$-module $S$ with nonzero quotient $(R/(u))[t]$, and the $t$'s stay regular on the polynomial quotients; if the pivot is some $t_a$, remove it first, leaving $R[t_l:l\ne a]$. Then [lem-trf-blowup-chart-regular-sequence-presentation] identifies the chart $S[(v_J)/v_a]$ with the ring $C$ of that lemma. Thus both product and blowup comparisons concern the actual local rings at the coordinate sections, not local rings at unrelated rational points after extending the ground field.

source.place: Tag 0C0S (lemma-regular-complete-containing-coefficient-field), plus the stated algebraic parameter-chart completion comparison, applied to the identified local rings.

proof.text: These maps compose with coefficients still fixed: define the field section at the next chart to be the image of the previous section under the actual completed local map. The comparison in step 11 identifies this with its constant field, so composition is literal substitution. For example adjoining $t$ and taking its chart gives $u_i\mapsto tu_i$, and repeating $k$ times gives $u_i\mapsto t^k u_i$; blowing up only $(t,u_1)$ changes just $u_1$. This is induction on the number of charts, using the explicit maps of step 11. If $n=0$, $R$ and $H$ are $F$, there are no boundary parameters on this support through $x$, and $(I_j)_x\subseteq\mathfrak m^{d_j}=0$ since $d_j\ge1$. Step 3 spreads the zero ideal. Near $x$ the finitely generated ideal of $T$ is zero, by the same denominator argument, so $T=N_j$ there. The zero-center blowup is empty by the $b=0$ case of [lem-trf-coordinate-subspace-blowup-charts]; there is no pivot chart to compare, whereas the product comparison still applies. Thus no step divides by a nonexistent parameter or excludes the zero-dimensional or nonclosed cases.

source.place: Tag 0804; zero-center case in coordinate-subspace blowup charts, and elementary composition of the explicit substitutions.
